title: Harness selection and execution
intro: Views of the harness-dispatch command and of Grove's use of it, matching the area specification's package, execution and original-creator topics. These are source-package and process views, not deployment containers. Graphs begin at a dark Start here node; sequence views begin at the first message.

groups.title: Package boundary
groups.description: One public command, an installed private worker, one owner policy, optional caller adapters.

groups.title: Execution and authority
groups.description: Selection ends before the foreground process becomes the harness. Grove runs the command for every session.

groups.title: Original creator and review
groups.description: A review carries a reference to its creator's run; run records outlive the task tree.

discussion.title: Grove launches through harness-dispatch; a policy returns the command
discussion.status: Designed in direct-dispatch-k3; its design review is integrated
discussion.summary: Grove has no launch configuration. A policy is one select function that receives the caller's parameters and the prompt and returns the command or a refusal. A confined grove run selects with inspect and launches the file it reports, looking nothing up again.

updatedDiagrams.summary: The policy returns a command instead of a catalog ID; owner settings and the optional choice file are new.
The request now carries the prompt, settings are read before the worker starts, and a policy may start a deciding agent.
New: Grove's lifecycle launch through run, and its confined standalone launch through inspect.
The provider is checked against the review entry's origins, not a catalog.
The run records the selected command's provider label; no candidate remains.
Option C's cost reworded: Grove reads nothing back from the dispatcher.

diagrams.title: Caller, dispatcher and policy packages
diagrams.caption: Source packages and runtime participants. The command holds no catalog: the owner's function returns the command. Grove-specific relationship parsing belongs to the optional adapter; the generic command has no review-kind list.

diagrams.title: Prepare, record and replace the foreground process
diagrams.caption: The worker shares the enclosing job and has null stdin. Cancellation or timeout before the handoff launches nothing. Keeping a deciding agent from executing the task it evaluates is its policy owner's job. Measurements after exec need an external observer.

diagrams.title: Grove's two launches: lifecycle and confined standalone
diagrams.caption: Grove passes the same data either way and reads no configuration. A lifecycle session is launched by run, which records and execs. A standalone invocation is selected by inspect, outside the sandbox, and launched by Grove's runner inside it, with no run record. The runner runs the file inspect resolved.

diagrams.title: Where each option keeps the creator's provider
diagrams.caption: The decision is A. A lookup keyed by handle must tell this grove's handle from an earlier grove's in the same workspace, which needs durable state Grove deliberately lacks (B). A globally unique run reference carried by the review needs none (A).

diagrams.title: Producer names its run; the review resolves it
diagrams.caption: The run reference is written by the session that ran under it, so the provider comes from dispatch's immutable record rather than a transcription. The association itself is that session's attestation, not verified. A session that finishes without a run removes any earlier line, and the owner declares the finished artifact's provider.

diagrams.title: Resolve the Creator line before selecting a reviewer
diagrams.caption: The supplied example policy. Every invocation and retry takes the same path; a retry reads the same line and the same immutable run, so it cannot change the creator.
